ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 2 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Joe Frazier

code.originalText: Two-week review of home blood pressure readings, with liver elastography, a liver ultrasound and the hepatology consultation

text.paragraph: Two-week review of home blood pressure readings, with liver elastography, ultrasound and hepatology. [S]

Mr. Frazier returns two weeks after intake with a week of home blood pressure readings, twice a day, averaging 146/90. He is taking metformin, lisinopril and the new atorvastatin without trouble. This morning he had liver elastography and a liver ultrasound, and he saw Dr. Deshpande of hepatology. He has had no swelling of the legs or abdomen, no black stools, no confusion and no yellowing. He drinks one or two beers on some weekends and agreed today to stop. He asked what a scarred liver means for his work at the gym. [S]

list.item:
Compensated cirrhosis from MASLD (K74.69). Liver stiffness 17.6 kPa with a controlled attenuation parameter of 318 dB/m; ultrasound shows a mildly nodular liver, a spleen of 13.4 cm and no focal lesion; AFP 4.2 ng/mL; INR 1.1; albumin 4.0 g/dL; bilirubin 0.9 mg/dL; platelets 138. Child-Pugh A (5 points), MELD 8. Hepatitis B surface antigen, core antibody and surface antibody negative; hepatitis A antibody negative; hepatitis C antibody and HIV test nonreactive; iron studies and autoimmune tests normal. Dr. Deshpande agrees this is compensated cirrhosis from MASLD, with little alcohol. [S]
Liver ultrasound with AFP every six months; the next in September.
Upper endoscopy to screen for varices, because platelets below 150 and a stiffness of 17.6 kPa cannot rule out portal hypertension.
No alcohol; no ibuprofen or naproxen; acetaminophen no more than 2 g a day.
PCV20 and first doses of hepatitis A and B vaccines today.

Type 2 diabetes, A1c 8.4% (E11.65). Above goal on metformin. A GLP-1 receptor agonist adds cardiovascular and kidney benefit and helps weight and steatotic liver disease; it is safe in compensated cirrhosis. Coverage approved after prior authorization. [S]
Start semaglutide 0.25 mg weekly for four weeks, then 0.5 mg weekly.
Continue metformin, safe with normal kidney function and compensated cirrhosis.
Diabetes self-management class booked.

Hypertension (I10). Home average 146/90 confirms blood pressure above the goal of 130/80 on lisinopril. [S]
Add amlodipine 5 mg daily.
Home readings twice a day for a week before the next visit.
